structural-causal.name: nuclear bottleneck control and substitution resilience
structural-causal.basis: uranium production plus fuel services and Westinghouse participation diversify value capture across the nuclear chain rather than relying on one commodity layer

discovery-weak-signals.name: nuclear fuel-cycle bottleneck exposure
discovery-weak-signals.basis: tier-one uranium assets, fuel services and Westinghouse exposure position Cameco across scarce nuclear supply-chain layers as contracting strengthens

adversarial-red-team.name: operational concentration and timing risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: remote-mine performance and project timing can create earnings volatility even with strong long-term contracting conditions

expectations-execution.name: balance-sheet and operating execution
expectations-execution.basis: strong liquidity and maintained annual guidance offset quarter-level production/logistics disruptions and lower Westinghouse equity earnings

factors: nuclear bottleneck control and substitution resilience

items.risk: Remote-mine disruptions, uranium delivery timing and Westinghouse project variability can produce volatile quarterly results.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA and Westinghouse contribution were below prior-year comparables, highlighting timing and project variability.
Successor bottlenecks may sit in enrichment, conversion, construction labor or reactor delivery rather than uranium, limiting how much upstream scarcity translates into value capture.
Cigar Lake ownership concentration increases exposure to a high-quality asset but also magnifies site-specific operational risk.
Westinghouse adds project and execution exposure distinct from uranium-market fundamentals.
